# Worlds Within

> Worlds Within is one persistent world played through many genres, and the engine that makes it. The repo is LLM-first: content is text, every run is repeatable from a seed, and tools let an agent check its own work. The engine (`engine/`) holds the loop, input, audio, graphics data, the presentation contract and backends; kits (`kits/`) hold one genre's gameplay rules and never draw (they describe each frame and a backend draws it through the game's skin); games (`games/`) hold content and depend on the engine and kits, never the other way round. Start with `CLAUDE.md` at the root, then the page for the module you are changing.

## Project

- [Root agent instructions](CLAUDE.md): rules every change must follow, and the checks to run before pushing
- [Design](docs/DESIGN.md): what the engine and the game are, and the dependency rule
- [Roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md): the release plan; check it before adding features
- [Stacking-test gap report](docs/reports/stacking-test.md): what Engine 0.7's test game found missing, 37 gaps, each fixed in 0.7 or moved to a named release, plus the glue review

## Modules

- [engine/core](docs/modules/engine-core.md): loop, scenes, input (keyboard, gamepad, touch pad, and from Engine 0.9 pointer gestures for mouse and touch: tap, box, pan, zoom), audio and MML, save, seeded RNG, maths, the renderer contract, the kit hook (`KitDef`), the mini game hook (`MiniGameDef` with an optional `paramsSchema` and `report()`, `miniGameScene`), the headless game contract (with optional recorded `order`s), the RTS order and unit-type data shared by the sim and kits (`orders.ts`, `rts-types.ts`), and from Engine 0.10 the mission contract (`missions.ts`: mission definitions and the `mission` content kind, declared outcomes, structured results and reports, `MissionAdapter`, and `mission-adapter.ts`: `playMissionRound` plays a mission through a kit's mini game and maps its report to a declared outcome)
- [engine/core/content](docs/modules/engine-core-content.md): content files read and checked with Zod schemas: text grids, song, sfx, sprite and palette schemas, game manifests (with the picture size, `screen`) and the content loader, errors naming the file and field
- [engine/core/present](docs/modules/engine-core-present.md): the presentation contract: the read-only per-frame snapshot (`PresentFrame`: entities, map, events, HUD status, camera and other extension points) a kit hands a backend, the `Presenter` interface, `freezeFrame`, `MapTracker`, the `presentFrameSchema` Zod schema, skin files (the `skin` content kind and `resolveSkinFrame`; `three` skins with text-defined low-poly meshes and `camera3d`), eight-way `Facing` (Engine 0.9), `CameraFollower`, the camera framing maths both backends share, `RtsCamera` (Engine 0.9: a scrolling, zooming camera over a map larger than the screen, with screen-to-world maths for pointer input), and `FrameStream` / `PendingEvents` / `FramePicture`, the per-frame stream from a world and its events to frozen frames
- [engine/core/shell](docs/modules/engine-core-shell.md): the browser shell games share: `?backend=` choice and the 2D/3D toggle, `HostScene` (plays a headless game and pushes its mini games), `bootBrowserGame` (keyboard, gamepad, touch pad, optional pointer gestures, scene stack, fixed loop) over a display a backend builds
- [engine/backends/canvas2d](docs/modules/engine-backends-canvas2d.md): the browser 2D backend, viewport, `SkinnedCanvasPresenter` (draws presentation frames through a skin, honouring the camera's zoom from Engine 0.9) and `canvasDisplay`, the page's 2D display
- [engine/backends/three](docs/modules/engine-backends-three.md): the 3D backend: `ThreeScene` builds a side-on 2.5D Three.js scene (instanced tile blocks, entity meshes by id, a perspective camera framed like the 2D one) from presentation frames and a `three` skin, testable in Node; `threeDisplay` (the page's 3D display, or why WebGL 2 is missing) and `threeScenePresenter` (a Node-side `Presenter`)
- [engine/backends/null](docs/modules/engine-backends-null.md): the headless backend that draws nothing (`NullRenderer`, `NullPresenter`)
- [engine/sim](docs/modules/engine-sim.md): the headless, deterministic world simulation (Engine 0.8): entities, components, fixed-order systems, a seeded RNG and an integer tick (one world minute); standard components, terrain with height and squads with named members; an event log of every committed change with its cause; save and load of the whole world as JSON; world scenarios as data and the sample village world; from Engine 0.9, in-house 8-way A\* and flow fields, RTS orders applied between ticks (`applyOrder`) and the RTS systems (movement, combat, construction, training, one gatherable resource) in a named system set (`"systems": "rts"`), with a recorded battle fixture; and deterministic integer and fixed-point maths (`math.ts`) in place of machine-dependent float maths
- [engine/tools](docs/modules/engine-tools.md): the CLI for agents and people (`pnpm cli help`): validate content, play run files headless with tick assertions, invariants and state hashes (and, from Engine 0.9, recorded orders with sync hashes, so a battle replays to the same hashes), write replay files for failing runs (with hash-mismatch checks), dump the state at a tick (of a game, or of a sim world from a `world` run file), edit content with get/set/add/remove (every write schema-checked and verified), mutant checks that switch kit rules off to find weak run files, deterministic PNG screenshots of a run at a tick (headless Chromium; `--backend three` for 3D, refusing software WebGL unless `--allow-software-gl`), with one JSON result per command and grouped exit codes
- [kits/topdown](docs/modules/kits-topdown.md): gameplay rules for a room-based top-down action game, with named rules a run can switch off; `presentWorld` describes each frame (map, entities, HUD status, events, camera hint); `roomChallenge` hosts one room as a mini game whose `report()` (Engine 0.10) says what was beaten and who was hurt; the kit never draws
- [kits/platformer](docs/modules/kits-platformer.md): gameplay rules for a side-scrolling platformer: `level` files (a JSON header plus a `.map.txt` text grid) and physics `profile` files in whole sub-pixel units with data-set actor types; integer physics and level objects as named rules (strict mutant checks), golden traces against SMBC, mini-game triggers; presentation frames (`presentWorld`); the kit never draws
- [kits/rts](docs/modules/kits-rts.md): the real-time strategy kit (Engine 0.9): reads a plain `engine/sim` world snapshot, turns click and box selection and commands into orders, runs a scripted enemy written as data, and describes each frame (map, units with eight-way facing, buildings and construction, selection, HUD, camera); no world rules, no drawing, no sim import
- [games/demo](docs/modules/games-demo.md): the proof-of-life demo game built on the top-down kit, drawn by the Canvas2D backend through its skin (`content/skins/canvas2d.json`)
- [games/platformer-lab](docs/modules/games-platformer-lab.md): the platformer kit's test lab: the kit's fixture level and five rule levels played in turn, run files that guard every kit rule, a placeholder Canvas2D skin and a low-poly 3D skin (`?backend=three` plays it through the Three.js backend), and a tiny test mini game
- [games/samples/rts-skirmish](docs/modules/games-samples-rts-skirmish.md): the first RTS sample (Engine 0.9): one map as a world scenario, unit and building types, a scripted raiding party as data, text pixel art and a Canvas2D skin, on `kits/rts` over `engine/sim`; run files build a barracks, train soldiers and beat the raid from recorded orders (and through interface actions) with sync hashes
- [games/platformer-test](docs/modules/games-platformer-test.md): the stacking test's game (Engine 0.7): a small original platformer on the platformer kit that finds what the engine is missing: four short levels and a door that pushes a top-down room challenge over the level, playable in 2D and 3D; a worked example of a game on two kits

## Reference

- [API cheat sheet](docs/CHEATSHEET.md): one page of the public API: a game's folder, booting a game, content kinds, the headless contract, run files and the CLI loop (its tables are generated)
- [CLI reference](docs/reference/cli.md): every command's help, exactly as `pnpm cli help` prints it (generated)
- [Schema reference](docs/reference/schemas.md): every file format (game manifest, run files, each content kind) with fields, types, defaults, limits and an example (generated)
- [Skills](docs/modules/skills.md): agent skills for common jobs, and how to add one

## Skills

- [Scaffold a game](.claude/skills/scaffold-game/SKILL.md): make a new one-room game in `games/<name>/` that passes `validate`, `run` and the four checks
- [Debug a failing run](.claude/skills/debug-failing-run/SKILL.md): from a failing `run` to its first failing tick, dumps, screenshot, replay and mutant checks, then fix and rerun
